evidence: Nestled in the heart of Hanoi, specifically at 58 Văn Miếu Street in Đống Đa District, lies the Temple of Literature, or Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám, a revered historical site that stands as a testament to Vietnam’s rich cultural heritage. Founded in 1070 under the reign of Emperor Lý Thánh Tông of the Lý dynasty, the Temple of Literature was initially established to honor Confucius, the great Chinese philosopher, and later evolved into Quốc Tử Giám, Vietnam’s first national university during the reign of Lý Nhân Tông.
